verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle, not from men nor through any man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from among the dead,
verses.1:2: and all the brethren with me, to the churches of Galatia:
verses.1:3: Grace be to you, and peace, from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.1:4: who gave Himself for our sins, so that He might rescue us out of the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
verses.1:5: to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.1:6: I marvel that you are so swiftly turning away from Him who called you in the grace of Christ to a different gospel,
verses.1:7: which is not another; only there are some who trouble you and desire to distort the gospel of Christ.
verses.1:8: Yet even if we, or an angel from heaven, should proclaim a gospel to you contrary to that which we proclaimed to you, let him be accursed.
verses.1:9: Just as we have said beforehand, now I also say again: if anyone proclaims a gospel to you contrary to that which you received, let him be accursed.
verses.1:10: For am I now striving to win over men, or God? Or do I seek to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I would not be a bondservant of Christ.
verses.1:11: For I make known to you, brethren, that the gospel proclaimed by me is not according to man;
verses.1:12: for neither did I receive it from any man, nor was I taught it, but it came by a revelation of Jesus Christ.
verses.1:13: For you have heard of my former manner of life in Judaism, how beyond measure I persecuted the church of God and sought to destroy it,
verses.1:14: and I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my own people, being abundantly more zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
verses.1:15: But when He who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me through His grace was pleased
verses.1:16: to reveal His Son in me, so that I might proclaim Him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood,
verses.1:17: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me; rather, I departed into Arabia, and returned once more to Damascus.
verses.1:18: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to become acquainted with Cephas, and I remained with him fifteen days.
verses.1:19: Yet I did not see any other of the apostles, except James, the brother of the Lord.
verses.1:20: Now in the things which I write to you, behold, before God, I do not lie.
verses.1:21: Then I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
verses.1:22: And I was still unknown in person to the churches of Judea which are in Christ;
verses.1:23: only they kept hearing, "He who formerly persecuted us now proclaims the faith which he once sought to destroy,"
verses.1:24: and they were glorifying God in me.
verses.2:1: Then after an interval of fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along as well.
verses.2:2: And I went up in accordance with a revelation, and I set before them the gospel that I proclaim among the Gentiles—yet privately to those of repute—lest somehow I should be running, or had run, in vain.
verses.2:3: But not even Titus, who was with me, though he was a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.
verses.2:4: Yet it was because of the false brethren secretly brought in, who stole in to spy out our liberty which we possess in Christ Jesus, so that they might bring us into bondage—
verses.2:5: to whom we did not yield in subjection even for an hour, so that the truth of the gospel might abide with you.
verses.2:6: And from those who were reputed to be something—whatever they once were makes no difference to me; God shows partiality to no man—for those who were of repute added nothing to me;
verses.2:7: but on the contrary, seeing that I had been entrusted with the gospel for the uncircumcised, just as Peter was for the circumcised
verses.2:8: (for He who worked powerfully in Peter for an apostleship to the circumcised worked also in me for the Gentiles),
verses.2:9: and recognizing the grace that had been given to me, James and Cephas and John, who were esteemed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
verses.2:10: Only they asked that we remember the poor—the very thing I also was diligent to do.
verses.2:11: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I withstood him to his face, because he stood condemned;
verses.2:12: for before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; yet when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, fearing those of the circumcision.
verses.2:13: And the rest of the Jews likewise acted hypocritically with him, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.
verses.2:14: But when I saw that they were not walking uprightly in accord with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before them all, "If you, being a Jew, live after the manner of the Gentiles and not after the manner of the Jews, how is it that you compel the Gentiles to live as Jews?"
verses.2:15: We ourselves are Jews by birth, and not sinners from among the Gentiles,
verses.2:16: yet knowing that a man is not justified by works of the law, but only through faith in Jesus Christ, we also have believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law; for by works of the law no flesh shall be justified.
verses.2:17: But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also were found to be sinners, is Christ therefore a minister of sin? May it never be!
verses.2:18: For if I rebuild the things which I tore down, I show myself to be a transgressor.
verses.2:19: For I through the law died to the law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ;
verses.2:20: and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me; and the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and delivered Himself up for me.
verses.2:21: I do not nullify the grace of God; for if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died in vain.
verses.3:1: O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was openly set forth as crucified?
verses.3:2: This alone I wish to learn from you: Did you receive the Spirit from works of the law, or from the hearing of faith?
verses.3:3: Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being brought to perfection in the flesh?
verses.3:4: Did you endure so many things in vain—if indeed it really was in vain?
verses.3:5: Therefore He who supplies the Spirit to you and works mighty deeds among you, does He do so from works of the law, or from the hearing of faith?
verses.3:6: Just as "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness."
verses.3:7: Know therefore that those who are of faith—these are the sons of Abraham.
verses.3:8: And the Scripture, foreseeing that God justifies the Gentiles by faith, proclaimed the gospel beforehand to Abraham, saying, "In you all the nations shall be blessed."
verses.3:9: Therefore those who are of faith are blessed together with faithful Abraham.
verses.3:10: For all who are of works of the law are under a curse; for it is written, "Cursed is everyone who does not abide in all the things written in the book of the law, to perform them."
verses.3:11: And that no one is justified by the law before God is evident, for "The righteous one shall live by faith."
verses.3:12: However, the law is not of faith; rather, "He who does them shall live in them."
verses.3:13: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse on our behalf (for it is written, "Cursed is everyone who hangs upon a tree"),
verses.3:14: in order that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that through faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit.
verses.3:15: Brethren, I speak according to human terms: even though it is only a man's covenant, once it has been ratified, no one sets it aside or adds to it.
verses.3:16: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, "And to seeds," as concerning many, but as concerning one, "And to your seed," who is Christ.
verses.3:17: Now this is what I say: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years afterward, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to abolish the promise.
verses.3:18: For if the inheritance comes from the law, it no longer comes from promise; yet God has graciously granted it to Abraham through a promise.
verses.3:19: Why then the law? It was added on account of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise had been made, having been ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.
verses.3:20: Now a mediator is not for one only, yet God is one.
verses.3:21: Is the law then contrary to the promises of God? By no means! For if a law had been given that was able to impart life, truly righteousness would have come from the law.
verses.3:22: Instead, the Scripture shut up all things under sin, in order that the promise from faith in Jesus Christ might be granted to those who believe.
verses.3:23: Now before faith came, we were guarded under the law, shut up until the faith that was to be revealed.
verses.3:24: Therefore the law has become our custodian until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
verses.3:25: Yet now that faith has come, we are no longer under a custodian.
verses.3:26: For all of you are sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:27: For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
verses.3:28: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bondservant nor free, there is no male and female; for all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:29: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's seed, heirs according to promise.
verses.4:1: Now I say this: for as long as the heir is a young child, he differs in nothing from a bondservant, though he is master of all,
verses.4:2: but he remains under guardians and stewards until the appointed time set by the father.
verses.4:3: In the same way we also, when we were young children, were held in bondage under the elemental principles of the world.
verses.4:4: Yet when the fullness of time arrived, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
verses.4:5: that He might redeem those who were under the law, in order that we might receive adoption as sons.
verses.4:6: And because you are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, "Abba, Father!"
verses.4:7: Therefore you are no longer a bondservant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir also through God.
verses.4:8: Formerly, indeed, when you did not know God, you were enslaved to those things which by nature are not gods.
verses.4:9: Yet now, having come to know God—or rather, having been known by God—how is it that you are turning back again to the weak and beggarly elemental principles, to which you wish to be enslaved once more?
verses.4:10: You closely observe days and months and seasons and years.
verses.4:11: I fear for you, lest somehow I have labored over you in vain.
verses.4:12: Become as I am, for I also became as you are, brethren, I implore you. You did me no wrong at all.
verses.4:13: Indeed, you know that it was on account of a weakness of the flesh that I proclaimed the gospel to you the first time;
verses.4:14: and what was a trial to you in my flesh you did not despise or loathe, but you welcomed me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
verses.4:15: Where then is your sense of blessedness? For I testify to you that, if it had been possible, you would have torn out your own eyes and given them to me.
verses.4:16: So then, have I become your enemy by speaking the truth to you?
verses.4:17: They are zealous for you, yet for no honorable end; rather, they desire to shut you out, so that you may be zealous for them.
verses.4:18: Yet it is always honorable to be zealous in an honorable cause, and not only when I am present with you,
verses.4:19: my children, for whom I am once more in the travails of childbirth until Christ is formed in you!
verses.4:20: Indeed, I could wish to be present with you right now and to alter my tone, for I am at a loss concerning you.
verses.4:21: Tell me, you who wish to be under the law, do you not hear the law?
verses.4:22: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the bondwoman and one by the free woman.
verses.4:23: Yet the one by the bondwoman was born according to the flesh, whereas the one by the free woman was born through promise.
verses.4:24: Now these things are spoken allegorically: for these women are two covenants—one from Mount Sinai, bearing children for bondage, which is Hagar.
verses.4:25: Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in bondage with her children.
verses.4:26: Yet the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
verses.4:27: For it is written: "Rejoice, O barren woman who does not give birth; break forth and cry aloud, you who are not in travail; for more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband."
verses.4:28: Now you, brethren, just as Isaac was, are children of promise.
verses.4:29: Yet just as at that time the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit, even so it is now.
verses.4:30: Yet what does the Scripture say? "Cast out the bondwoman and her son, for the son of the bondwoman shall by no means inherit together with the son of the free woman."
verses.4:31: Therefore, brethren, we are not children of a bondwoman, but of the free woman.
verses.5:1: For liberty Christ has set us free; stand steadfast, therefore, and do not again be held fast by a yoke of bondage.
verses.5:2: Behold, I, Paul, declare to you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will be of no profit to you.
verses.5:3: And again I bear solemn witness to every man who receives circumcision that he is a debtor to perform the entire law.
verses.5:4: You have been cut off from Christ, all you who strive to be justified by law; you have fallen away from grace.
verses.5:5: For by the Spirit, out of faith, we earnestly await the hope of righteousness.
verses.5:6: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is of any avail, but faith working through love.
verses.5:7: You were running well; who impeded you from obeying the truth?
verses.5:8: Such persuasion is not from Him who calls you.
verses.5:9: A little leaven leavens the entire batch of dough.
verses.5:10: I am confident concerning you in the Lord that you will adopt no other mind; yet he who unsettles you shall bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
verses.5:11: But as for me, brethren, if I still proclaim circumcision, why am I still persecuted? In that case the stumbling block of the cross has been abolished.
verses.5:12: I wish that those who throw you into turmoil would even mutilate themselves!
verses.5:13: For you were called to liberty, brethren; only do not make this liberty an occasion for the flesh, but through love be servants to one another.
verses.5:14: For the entire law stands fulfilled in a single saying, in this: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
verses.5:15: Yet if you keep biting and devouring one another, take heed lest you be consumed by one another.
verses.5:16: Now I say, walk by the Spirit, and you shall by no means carry out the desire of the flesh.
verses.5:17: For the flesh sets its desire against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; for these stand opposed to one another, so that you do not perform the very things you wish.
verses.5:18: Yet if you are being led by the Spirit, you are not under law.
verses.5:19: Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these: sexual immorality, uncleanness, licentiousness,
verses.5:20: idolatry, sorcery, enmities, strife, jealousies, outbursts of fury, selfish rivalries, dissensions, factions,
verses.5:21: envyings, bouts of drunkenness, revelries, and things like these; concerning which I forewarn you, even as I warned you before, that those who practice such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.
verses.5:22: Yet the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
verses.5:23: meekness, self-control; against things such as these there is no law.
verses.5:24: Now those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh together with its passions and cravings.
verses.5:25: If we live by the Spirit, by the Spirit let us also order our steps.
verses.5:26: Let us not become vainglorious, challenging one another, envying one another.
verses.6:1: Brethren, even if a man is overtaken in some transgression, you who are spiritual, restore such a one in a spirit of meekness, keeping watch over yourself, lest you also be tempted.
verses.6:2: Carry one another's burdens, and thus you shall fulfill the law of Christ.
verses.6:3: For if anyone supposes himself to be something while being nothing, he deludes his own mind.
verses.6:4: Rather, let each one scrutinize his own work, and then he shall have cause for boasting in himself alone, and not in regard to another;
verses.6:5: for each one shall carry his own load.
verses.6:6: Now let the one who is instructed in the word share in all good things with the one who instructs him.
verses.6:7: Do not be led astray: God is not mocked; for whatever a man sows, this very thing he shall also reap;
verses.6:8: because he who sows to his own flesh shall reap corruption from the flesh, whereas he who sows to the Spirit shall reap eternal life from the Spirit.
verses.6:9: And let us not lose heart in doing what is good, for in the appointed season we shall reap, if we do not grow faint.
verses.6:10: So then, while we have opportunity, let us perform what is good toward all people, and above all toward those who belong to the household of faith.
verses.6:11: Behold with what large letters I write to you with my own hand.
verses.6:12: All who desire to make a fair display in the flesh, these compel you to receive circumcision, solely so that they may not be persecuted on account of the cross of Christ.
verses.6:13: For not even those who have been circumcised themselves keep the law; rather, they desire you to receive circumcision so that they may boast in your flesh.
verses.6:14: Yet may it never be that I should boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world stands crucified to me, and I to the world.
verses.6:15: For neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision, but rather a new creation.
verses.6:16: And for all who shall order their walk by this rule, peace be upon them and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
verses.6:17: From this time forward, let no one cause me trouble, for I bear in my body the brand marks of Jesus.
verses.6:18: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brethren. Amen.

notes.1:6: In verses 6-7, Paul contrasts "a different gospel" (heteron) with "another" (allo), underscoring that any distortion of the message of Christ is no true gospel at all.
notes.1:15: The Greek critical text reads literally "He who set me apart," without the explicit noun "God" found in later manuscripts, though God is clearly the implied subject.
notes.1:18: The verb historesai denotes visiting someone to become personally acquainted and inquire of them; "Cephas" is the Aramaic name of the apostle Peter.
notes.2:4: Verses 4-5 reflect an abrupt grammatical break (anacoluthon) in the Greek text as Paul interrupts his sentence to denounce the intrusion of the false brethren.
notes.2:15: Many interpreters regard Paul's address to Cephas begun in verse 14 as continuing through verse 21, moving from the Antioch incident into a broader theological defense of justification by faith.
notes.2:16: The Greek phrase pistis Christou ("faith in Christ") is grammatically capable of being read either as an objective genitive ("faith in Christ") or a subjective genitive ("the faithfulness of Christ"); the same construction recurs in verse 20.
notes.2:19: The clause "I have been crucified with Christ" stands at the end of verse 19 in the critical Greek text, whereas many older English translations place it at the beginning of verse 20.
notes.3:1: The critical Greek text reads the shorter form without "that you should not obey the truth" and "among you," which appear in later manuscripts.
notes.3:20: Paul's concise statement contrasts the indirect, multi-party mediation of the law at Sinai with the direct, unilateral promise made by the one God to Abraham.
notes.3:22: The Greek phrase ἐκ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ is debated and may be understood either as "from faith in Jesus Christ" (objective genitive) or "from the faithfulness of Jesus Christ" (subjective genitive).
notes.3:24: Greek παιδαγωγός refers to a household custodian or guardian who supervised a minor child's conduct and escorted him to school, rather than a classroom teacher.
notes.4:3: Greek τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου ("the elemental principles of the world") is debated and may denote rudimentary religious principles, basic cosmic elements, or spiritual powers governing the present age.
notes.4:7: The critical Greek text reads διὰ θεοῦ ("through God"), whereas later manuscripts expand the phrase to "of God through Christ."
notes.4:14: The critical Greek text reads τὸν πειρασμὸν ὑμῶν ("what was a trial to you"), whereas later manuscripts read "my trial."
notes.4:25: The neuter article in τὸ δὲ Ἁγὰρ treats the name "Hagar" itself as the grammatical subject, linking her allegorically to Mount Sinai in Arabia and the present Jerusalem.
notes.5:12: The Greek verb apokopsontai ("mutilate themselves" or "cut themselves off") carries sharp irony in a dispute over circumcision, alluding to the self-emasculation practiced in Anatolian pagan cults.
notes.5:19: In this catalog of the works of the flesh (5:19-21), the critical Greek text omits "adultery" in verse 19 and "murders" in verse 21, both of which appear in later Byzantine manuscripts.
notes.5:24: The critical Greek text reads "Christ Jesus" here rather than "Christ" alone as in later manuscripts.
notes.6:2: Greek bare ("burdens") refers to heavy, crushing loads shared in fellowship, contrasted with phortion ("load" or personal pack) in verse 5; the critical text also reads the future indicative "you shall fulfill" rather than an imperative.
notes.6:11: Greek egrapsa ("I write") is an epistolary aorist marking the point where Paul takes the pen himself to write in large letters, whether for solemn emphasis or because of weak eyesight.
notes.6:15: The critical Greek text reads simply "neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision," without the phrase "in Christ Jesus" found in later Byzantine manuscripts.
notes.6:16: The conjunction kai ("and") before "upon the Israel of God" may be taken either additively (referring to believing Israel alongside Gentile believers) or epexegetically ("even upon the Israel of God") to identify all who walk by this rule.
